claims.claim: Reviewers report that base structures and the starting area become submerged and flooded as the terraforming progress advances and water levels rise.

citations.review_text:
the base game's gameplay loop feels similar to a roblox tycoon. you gather resources, create machinery to increase terraformation index, heat, oxygen and a few other metrics. then you rinse and repeat and mine better ores and materials until you get better tools and equipment to reach a milestone such as launching rockets or driving ATVs. 

while i only have 9 hours so far the game just seems boring since your only obstacles to progression is time itself since the machinery has to generate heat/oxygen or whatever to progress and there's no combat or any sort of impending doom/peril to worry about at all. all you have to worry about is your oxygen running low. even then its just a matter of mining resources to get larger oxygen tanks and more efficient movement methods/mining speed to alleviate the issue. 

the only "perilous" thing there even is to worry about really is relocating your base when the world floods.

ts fye js make sure to build a lil past the triangle rocks cuz when u start gettin water the spot where u first landed is gonna get flooded (sayin this as someone currently recycling their old house into a stilt house) im js tryna save whoever i can from havin to wreck their entire build n restart like me

If your a fan of intuitive controls and convenient gameplay features do not buy this game. Its fun and has potential for me to play it more but the amount of little things that irk me about this game piled up so much i couldn't not leave a bad review. the UI closes you out of it every time you place an object in build mode or craft something. the foundations and rooms are different sizes and tile in strange ways making for uneven, sloppy looking bases no matter how you build. there's no way to snap like half the structures in the game to a grid so it will always look awkward when you place lots of the same thing in one spot unless you spend 10 minutes making it "perfect" every time. you cant change the settings for a world after creation so if you decide you wanna change something i hope you know how to edit save files. almost all of the early progression relies on exploration but with how aggressive the vitals are on even the standard difficulty it feels punishing to explore unless you fill half your inventory with food, water, and oxygen and then your forced to make several trips. maybe i could have forgiven all of that but the thing that really broke me was needing to pick up and move my entire base because the 4th milestone is filling the planet with lakes and the starting drop pod that i built next to happens to be at the bottom of one of these lakes meaning you must build away from the starting area or you will be flooded very early on. with how good the reviews were for this game I honestly expected much more and found myself disappointed during many sections of this experience.

I didnt buy the DLCs but i 100% will. i play this alone and its such a chill game to play, it might be fun with others but i dont want anyone coming in and messing up my world ! like GET OUT! 
you will get lost in this game, hours will pass, children will go hungry, partners unloved.

Like subnautica (90%) and a clicker (10%)  had a baby.

Land on a planet. Collect resources and build machines to help terraform the planet into a livable utopia.  The "Clicker" part is mainly in that 3 different buildings contribute to an ever-ticking up number that is the "Terraform Index". Recommended

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that the inventory system does not allow items to stack, requiring players to manage limited space carefully.

citations.review_text:
So I know I currently have only 6 hours in this game, but that's enough for what I have to say, which is also confirmed by other negative reviews. I, too, don't understand why this game is "overwhelmingly positive" and has so many glowing reviews like it's the second coming, because it's very mediocre and overrated with low-quality graphics, clumsy menus, and lots of glitches and tedious mechanics.

I was looking forward to something as rich as Subnautica (which I have spent hundreds of hours playing and modding) but with a focus on terraforming, but within a few hours, I was already bored to death and felt my time was being wasted as the game turns into another tedious item-collection walking simulator with arbitrarily restrictive "survival" mechanics. Resources are just scattered everywhere on the surface of this low-poly PS2-looking planet, and the wrecks are all very similar after you explore the first one. You will spend most of your time moving crap back and forth in a limited inventory while you watch screens and wait for number to go up to randomly unlock new things to make number go up. I literally do not have time for this, and do not want to spend my limited recreation time doing something so boring. It's insulting that modern game design has come to treating its' players like hamsters in a wheel.

I do not understand "modern" gamers or anyone that thinks this is fun and not a boring waste of their time. Apparently people just have so much free time and so low of standards that anything barely functional that allows them to click button and receive even the most minor dopamine hit will quality as le OVERWHELMINGLY POSITIVE GREAT GAME! I feel conned by these endless glowing reviews of this below-average game that plays like an indie alpha release made by one person that ripped off Subnautica assets but not any of its' actual fun or immersion.

For the money they charge for this, you could buy Subnautica, or Factorio, or Satisfactory, or any other number of…

They fixed everything that made me always get bored with minecraft. Although you have to explore and gather resources the survial mechanics are way more realistic and since items dont stack you have to be efficent and prioritise what you build first. Also unlocking new tiers of tech and having goals always gives you something to do and even on low settings the game looks great and seeing the planet slowly change is very satisfying

great game, albiet a little slow at times. 9.5/10 progression can be tedious

This game is basically a lesser Subnautica that is also much more grindier. The amount of time you waste picking terribly rendered elements from the ground and chasing (disappearing) elements from asteroids are enormous.

There are no real stakes in the game past early game. All kinds of game mechanics are very simplified. You can just build any power generator anywhere on the planet, it will magically connect to your invisible grid and power your stuff for example. 

The objective of the game is: You want a number to go up and it will go up, that's it. You build machines and then you build more machines just to make various numbers go up. It's super repetitive.

Something that really grated me was constantly finding loot boxes even at very remote locations that are clearly there to reward the player for exploring that point. The existence of these boxes give the game a theme park feeling rather than a survival environment where you're terraforming a planet to save yourself. At some point, you end up relying these kinds of loot boxes for efficient access to rarer elements of advanced materials and that sucks because they are not a renewable resource (your other option typically  is to grind harder).

On the positive side, seeing the planet change as you terraform it more and more is cool. You can also discover a bunch of stuff, which was interesting. Ultimately, I don't feel like there is enough meat on the bones though...

Planet Crafter is in its 2.0 state, but it still feels closer to an early access game than a fully polished release.

The UI is extremely bland and functional, and visually the game feels dated and unappealing for something centered around transforming a planet over time.

Survival mechanics also lose tension surprisingly quickly. Early on, food can be scarce, but death ends up having almost no consequence. If you die inside an oxygenated area, you simply respawn there. Since exploration lets you carry the materials needed to build an oxygenated shelter almost anywhere, you can effectively create a checkpoint whenever you want. We often ended up intentionally dying to refill needs instead of managing food and water, because there’s little reason not to.

Progression is mixed. The opening hours feel slow and grind-heavy, but unlocking new technologies and seeing your capabilities expand eventually becomes satisfying.

Overall, I found the game more tedious than engaging. A lot of the experience feels like completing repetitive tasks rather than meaningful survival or exploration. If you enjoy methodical resource gathering and incremental progression, there’s something here but for me, it felt more like doing chores than playing a game.

claims.claim: Reviewers report performance stuttering issues during the late stages of the game.

citations.review_text:
This game turns Subnautica on its head by turning it into a factory game.
It's overall a very chill experience, one that I can get lost with friends in for much more time than anticipated. It's got a vast amount of different things for you to do, especially in later stages of the game, where it introduces things like automation and a variety of ways to progress your terraformation progress. Alongside a story and lore that continues to make me set sights beyond the horizon and continue forth into the unknown, despite my constantly depleting status bars.
Definitely reccomend this game, especially if you and some friends like Subnautica and want something fresh (especially while waiting for Subnautica 2 updates...)
The game overall is incredibly performant most of the time, especially on low graphics. Although it does stutter here or there, particularly in dense pre-generated environments. (Especially that ONE secret area (Those who know))

Oh and the references some achievements have to other games is cute and more games should do that I think cause its awesome

This was a fun game for what it was, and I enjoyed it, but I have some major gripes which need to be addressed and shown to new players who think that due to the rating on this game that it will be as good as games like Satisfactory or Subnautica. Unfortunately, it doesn't quite hold a candle to those games in several areas despite clearly taking inspiration from them. I'll list the problems I had in order of greatest to least impactful:

- The game has performance issues. It has been known there are stuttering issues which have been "fixed", which make the game extremely hard to play in the late stages of the game. It took the game almost 30 hours to start doing this, but it made my final 10 hours unbearable at times and made me avoid doing any dlc or moons. Other than that it runs at a high framerate for me, but the stuttering was unpredictable and unsolvable. 

- The game is buggy in some aggravating areas which are hard to predict. For some reason after a certain point, the gravity on my planet stopped functioning and I would have moments of extremely light gravity which would slow my movement to a crawl. This, along with jetpack movement being a little janky itself, made moving around had my screen jumping so much it gave me a headache.

- The game really does not have a good color scheme to look at in the first 10-20 hours. It's one thing to have a desert, many games have that. Somehow the color the devs chose is one that will actively fatigue your eyes. I'm unsure if it's how few shadows are present due to no atmosphere, and it does get considerably easier to look at as you terraform, but 20 hours of bright orange sand makes me hate it about as much as anakin.

- I really would've liked to see more done to the points of interest and more care shown to the storybuilding. It feels like every cool area stops just as it could offer something better. Very few of them felt great to finally unlock and didn't offer anything that felt like I was rewarded.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that buildings and foundation pieces use mismatched grids, making placement frustrating.

citations.review_text:
I really enjoy exploration and building games, especially building. This game is lovely and has interesting progression. I love how the landscape changes and the leveling up/QoL are satisfying. I've very much enjoyed it and I give it a thumbs up, but with one reservation.... building. Which is a big deal because, as far as I can tell at this point, exploring and building are the game. That's 50% of the game which is not working for me right now.

[Slight spoilers ahead] 

There is a chance that I haven't unlocked options that will fix this (the farthest I've gotten is fish and accessing/powering/looting every wreck I've found on the map), but for right now building is incredibly frustrating. The buildings and the foundation pieces use different grids. If you've played it you know what I'm talking about, if not, get ready for a much less smooth experience with building than other games of this type. (ie Grounded, Subnautica, Windrose, The Forest - all have more flexible and friendly processes for building.) 

I'd rate this game 10/10 if the building wasn't so janky. Maybe it'll get better as I advance, or maybe I'll eventually understand how to handle the mismatched grids. I'll keep trying, but really wish the devs would either align the grids or let us fine adjust building placement. It's a significant drawback and I could see it leading to a less determined player to bail on the game. When building is all you have to do, and it doesn't work... welp.

ETA: I just went back in and here's an example. I'm working only with foundations and want to make a parking garage kind of structure. I have ramps up toward the north connecting to flats. I extend the flats to the east and then try to ramp up heading back to the south. The southward ramps I try to add will not snap. In fact, the game assumes added ramps will go up to the north no matter which way I face when I hit Q. What even is happening with this game?

Good game, something I can just unwind with and turn off the brain while gathering resources. Looks great too and performs well, plus the building is cozy, exploring and terraforming tasks are well balanced, and despite a couple minor inconsistencies with building such as the railing not snapping fully to the ground when building on the roof, it's a solid game.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that technological progress and unlocked blueprints carry over across planets in a single save file, which can bypass the survival and struggle aspects when starting new planets later.

citations.review_text:
Recommended
OS: Linux mint
Memory: ddr3 16GB
CPU: I-7 4790
GPU: Radeon RX 6600 XT
End game frame rate 50-60 fps

Overall, an amazing terraforming and survival game that runs flawlessly on Linux via Proton. However, there is one massive design flaw regarding the DLCs and multiple planets.

The game links your technological progress and unlocked blueprints to your main save file, not the individual planet. If you start on Selenea or Humble and finish it, flying to Prime afterwards completely ruins the core gameplay loop. You arrive with endgame tech, completely bypassing the struggle and survival aspect that makes this game great. The transition feels like a cheat mode rather than a new challenge.

The developers desperately need to implement a way to reset blueprint progression when traveling to a new planet, or isolate the tech trees. Until then, you are forced to start a completely new save file for each planet if you want the true survival experience.

Still highly recommended, but keep this progression flaw in mind when buying the DLCs.

Good game overall.
The progression is challenging and mostly makes sense. I've spent 80-ish hours playing across 3 planets/moons (Prime/Humble/Selenea).  There are two things I do not like and they are enough to make me give up on the game until/unless they are changed.
1. All items are limited to a stack size of 1.  Inventory size starts at 12 and goes up by 4 as you add larger backpacks, so not very big.  This makes you run back and forth across the map several times to build up a satellite base.  All the running is pointless and VERY boring.
2. Because of #1, I installed a mod to increase stack size.  Unfortunately, this breaks drone automation.  It seems they are not capable of reliably dealing with more than one item in an inventory slot.  They work for a few minutes after a load but then stop.  I am definitely not going to run all over the place endlessly, so broken automation results in me not playing any more.

YMMV if you don't mind all the running with nothing to do in between.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game features automation elements like drones and auto-crafters to handle logistics and resource gathering later in the game.

citations.review_text:
Planet Crafter is a fun survival game with solid progression elements. Most survival games allow you to shape the world around you as you play, Planet Crafter turns it up to 11 by literally having you transform the planet from barren to full of life.

The survival elements are solid, but where the game really shines is designing your base and increasing your terraforming. The futuristic base elements, screens, and tech all make for a very fun design motif. I do wish there was more science involved: I'd love to take core samples, water samples, really shape the direction of the terraforming on Prime in order to increase late-game mechanics.

Automation from drones and auto-crafters are great, though it'd be nice to have some quality of life options like copy/paste for storage, and presets like Trees, Food Seeds, etc so we can just select a general grouping to avoid slowly adding 10 plus items to filters. It would also be nice if the world was more interactive, but since there is no threat of violence I understand why creatures don't do much.

Overall: 90/100

The first time I plaid this, I took the freeware demo. It hooked me so much, that I took the game few days after. 

The sheer amount of potential of this game is huge. I firmly believe, that over the years will become the best game of it's kind. 

1. Graphics - perfect. 
2. Performance - perfect, unless the clutter become too much, then you start losing it. 
3. The challenge is quite educational, gets you out of zone of comfort so easily, that you will gasp each time when something bad happens. 
4. Most of the time Oxygen will be the biggest problem, until you reach " breathable atmosphere" on each planet / moon in the game. however, with time the oxygen tank will become bigger, stronger and help you survive, until it becomes eternal at the stage I mentioned up. However, EVEN THEN when you decide to swim, for example, to reach the Cenote, you will need oxygen bottles. Also underwater wrecks. 
5. Objects - you start with simple mining on a death planet, basically. Sand storms, meteors and a lot of oxygen losing for short period of time. Overtime, however, the recipes will become more complicated, you will need to nonstop explore, nonstop upgrade, nonstop increase your chances of survival. At certain point you will need huge pile of storage closets, filled with numbers of things, you will have to keep nonstop produce. 
6.  Logistics - drones will help you get all the clutter from the wreckages you did not managed, will take care of algae, water, honey, veggies and everything else - building ecosystem. 
7. This game is an EDUCATIONAL game to me, because it actually teaches you about what's important - keeping the life of the planet. Transforming it with technology, creating biosphere good enough, so you can survive. 
Trading rockets will help you. The advantages are much more then those, just too much text!

Few con's:

1. Performance becomes heavy once the world is developed. I see there is an effort, so I will be patient. 
2. Clutter is too much sometimes, even with …

A wonderfully zen game where your only enemies are your environment.  As you bend the environment to suit your needs, it becomes increasingly beautiful and filled with life.  There's a good balance between exploration, hand crafting, and automation.  Unlike some other games in the genre, this rarely feels like a grind.

DLC content is fun, too, though early game on each new planet feels very similar.

My only complaint is the clunkiness of automated interplanetary logistics, especially when learning how to properly configure things (since the documentation on this isn't very clear).

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the early game as requiring resource management and survival pressure regarding oxygen, thirst, and food, which eases as players upgrade and progress.

Fun first person base-builder. Even without external threats (e.g. zombies, raids), the different zones, biomes, and space wrecks are quite fun to explore.

There is survival pressure, especially early in the game, due to lack of food, water, and oxygen, but these are overcome later as you progress and upgrade. There is some grinding early on as well (collecting resources) but these get automated later. The progression makes sense and is successful in keeping you engaged.

(8/10)

claims.claim: Reviewers report that multiplayer is limited by a lack of cross-platform support and public game browsing.

citations.review_text:
Think twice before buying this game for a PC - particually if you are in Australia and you like multiplayer. 
.
Once you get deeper into the game - every aspect of all that is around you has to be loaded from the 'Steam Cloud' which is often fustratingly very slow. I have a high end dedicated PC with a suitable highend graphics card - connected to a highspeed fiber optic cable internet connection.
.
Over 1/4 of the time (if not 1/3 of it) that I have played this game - has been frustratingly spent waiting for the next bit of graphics etc etc to load from the 'Steam Cloud'
.
I actually play another simpler game on another computer while I wait for the 'next bit' to load for this game. Even just saving or exiting the game is very slow and painfull. 
.
The Multiplayer system is far more limited than Steam or the devlopers will ever tell you. It does not support cross-platform multiplayer even with PC type/based consoles and the multiplayer systen does not tell you if there are even any games you may be able to join out there.
.
It could be great - if it wasnt so slow and all people could play together or join a public game. 
.
If you have plenty of time to waste and only want to play single player - then the game may be worth it to you. It has a decent backstory and plenty to do and find (once it loads the next bit)

Very good game just one problem (That they are most likely already working on) no crossplay. So for now don't have any friends or family members that want to play with you but have different consoles buy this until crossplay is released. Other than that i highly recommend this game.
